children: Shares of Borr Drilling fell after the company said it is searching for five individuals who remain unaccounted for following an incident involving its Prospector 5 drilling rig offshore Gabon.
The stock declined 7.5%, to $4.07, in premarket trading Monday. Through Friday's close, shares are up more than 10% year to date.

Borr Drilling said the incident involving the Prospector 5 drilling rig occurred Saturday. Preliminary information indicated the rig experienced a punch through event, in which the base of one the rig's leg penetrates beyond its intended depth, resulting in a sudden loss of stability and the subsequent sinking of the rig.

At the time of the incident, there were 115 personnel onboard the rig, the company said. A total of 110 individuals had been safely accounted for as of Sunday. Search and rescue operations are continuing for the five remaining individuals.

Borr Drilling said its onshore emergency response team continues to work with local authorities in response to the incident, including to ensure an investigation is carried out into the cause of the incident.

"We are deeply concerned for those who remain unaccounted for and everyone affected by this incident," Chief Executive Bruno Morand said. He added that the company's immediate priority is to support search and rescue efforts and the welfare of all personnel involved.
